scope: Three royal-wedding v2 corrections viewed at original detail against rejected originals.
globalConditions: Only these new hashes pass; review 35 and its rejected original hashes remain unchanged.
Technical source/visual review is not owner approval or final browser acceptance.

entries.alt: Two distinct servants in cream tunics speak with people beside a road, one gesturing toward a distant columned entrance.
entries.caption: The servants go out to the roads and gather everyone they find. The king's invitation reaches beyond the original guests, and the wedding hall begins to fill.
entries.findings: Older balding left servant now clearly differs from younger curly-haired right servant. Natural reciprocal attention and coherent open hands, bundle grip and staff grip. Distant entrance is now a plain columned ancient-style portico, with former heraldry removed. Photographic faces and materials preserved.
conditions: Do not identify the crowd's moral standing from appearance or claim these are the identical two servants in scene 01.

entries.alt: A varied group of guests shares food and conversation at crowded banquet tables beneath plain hanging cloths.
entries.caption: The wedding hall is filled with guests gathered by the servants. Faces turn toward one another around the tables, picturing the breadth of the invitation in Jesus' story.
entries.findings: Central guest is now an older balding clean-shaven man, clearly distinct from the approved Christ likeness. Heraldic lion banners replaced by plain textiles; simpler garments retain banquet atmosphere without the earlier strong medieval cues. Cups, food contact, hands and reciprocal social attention remain coherent and photographic.
conditions: No Jesus figure is identified within the parable; exact banquet furnishings and costumes are illustrative.

entries.alt: A king wearing a simple circlet and dark green cloak addresses a plainly dressed man among the banquet guests.
entries.caption: The king notices a guest without a wedding garment and asks how he entered. The man has no answer. Jesus' story holds the wide invitation together with the seriousness of responding to it.
entries.findings: Plain circlet, layered woven cloak and restrained trim replace the conspicuously medieval royal costume. Heraldic banners removed. King and guest retain distinct faces, appropriate seriousness, reciprocal gaze and coherent open-palm and lowered-hand anatomy. No new material visual issue.
conditions: Do not explain the missing garment as poverty or assert an unrecorded custom of the king supplying garments.
The king is an unnamed parable character, not a literal portrait of God.
